variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Private capital outpaces federal awards
variants.takeaway: The gap may partly reflect the dual-use nature of many Aus NatSec50 companies, which serve both commercial and government markets. However, it also points to the need for government to turn national security demand into procurement contracts that generate sustained revenue and help these companies scale.
variants.descriptor: Cumulative private capital raised and federal award value

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: The capital-to-awards gap widens
variants.takeaway: CDC’s large federal awards mask a wider gap across the rest of the cohort. Without CDC, private capital is 7.1 times federal award value, reinforcing the need to turn national security demand into sustained procurement revenue.
variants.descriptor: Cumulative private capital raised and federal award value

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Procurement now outweighs recorded grant support
variants.takeaway: The balance of federal support has shifted sharply towards contract notices as recorded grant value has declined. The distinction matters: grants and procurement represent different forms of government engagement with the ecosystem.
variants.descriptor: Federal contract-notice and grant value by financial year (AUD millions)

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: The shift towards procurement extends beyond CDC
variants.takeaway: The move towards contract notices is still visible after removing the largest award recipient. Procurement value rose in the latest completed financial year while grant value fell sharply, changing the mix of federal support.
variants.descriptor: Federal contract-notice and grant value by financial year (AUD millions)

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Large awards reshape the federal buyer mix
variants.takeaway: Including CDC changes the FY2024–25 picture significantly: a AU$226.2 million Services Australia contract makes that agency the largest buyer. CDC’s Home Affairs awards also move that agency into first place in FY2025–26.
variants.descriptor: Federal award value by buyer and financial year (AUD millions)

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Defence anchors federal demand
variants.takeaway: Defence is the largest federal buyer in every year shown, with its share reaching 82% in FY2025–26. Other agencies contribute meaningful support, but the overall pattern centres on defence demand.
variants.descriptor: Federal award value by buyer and financial year (AUD millions)

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Data infrastructure shapes procurement language
variants.takeaway: The prominence of data and centre terminology places infrastructure-related work at the forefront of recorded contract titles. Equipment and software also feature strongly, pointing to a mix of physical and digital procurement.
variants.descriptor: Most frequent terms in federal contract-notice titles

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Products and supporting work both feature in procurement
variants.takeaway: Equipment and software lead the contract-title vocabulary after CDC is removed, alongside research and support. The pattern points to a mix of technical products and supporting work rather than a single type of purchase.
variants.descriptor: Most frequent terms in federal contract-notice titles

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: A few purchase categories dominate contract value
variants.takeaway: Engineering, data services and property leases together account for more than three-quarters of recorded contract value. The mix shows why aggregate procurement figures cannot be interpreted solely as purchases of emerging technology products.
variants.descriptor: Federal contract-notice count and value by procurement category

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Research leads procurement beyond CDC
variants.takeaway: Military science and research becomes the largest purchase category once CDC is removed. Categories with few notices can still carry substantial value, so frequent purchases and large financial commitments do not necessarily indicate the same priorities.
variants.descriptor: Federal contract-notice count and value by procurement category

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: AUKUS technology tags capture only part of the ecosystem
variants.takeaway: Companies outside the six recorded AUKUS technology categories hold most of the cohort’s capital and contract value. The classification therefore captures a narrower slice of the ecosystem than its full national security relevance.
variants.descriptor: Company, private-capital and federal-contract shares by AUKUS capability

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Advanced cyber stands out in federal procurement
variants.takeaway: Advanced cyber’s share of contract value is much larger than its share of companies once CDC is removed. Meanwhile, companies outside the recorded AUKUS categories remain prominent in private investment, illustrating different concentrations of capital and government demand.
variants.descriptor: Company, private-capital and federal-contract shares by AUKUS capability

variants.label: Original
variants.title: AI and autonomy lead recorded AUKUS representation
variants.takeaway: AI and autonomy is the most common recorded AUKUS capability, followed by quantum technologies. Half the cohort falls outside these six categories, underscoring that AUKUS technology tags do not capture every company’s national security relevance.
variants.descriptor: Company representation by recorded AUKUS technology area

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Information technologies lead capital and federal awards
variants.takeaway: Including CDC puts information and communications first on both financial measures. CDC alone accounts for about 45% of private capital and 70% of federal award value, making a single infrastructure provider decisive to the category’s lead.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by critical technology area

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Autonomy leads capital and federal awards
variants.takeaway: Clean energy holds more than a quarter of private capital but less than 6% of federal awards. The contrast with autonomy’s lead across both measures shows how differently private investment and government support are distributed across technology areas.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by critical technology area

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Company breadth and financial scale diverge
variants.takeaway: Autonomy, robotics and sensing has the broadest company representation, while information and communications dominates private capital and federal awards. Counting companies alone therefore gives a different picture of the ecosystem from measuring its financial scale.
variants.descriptor: Company, private-capital and federal-award shares by critical technology area

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Autonomy leads across three measures
variants.takeaway: Without CDC, autonomy, robotics and sensing leads company representation, private capital and federal awards. Its larger share of awards than of companies suggests stronger concentration in government support than in company presence.
variants.descriptor: Company, private-capital and federal-award shares by critical technology area

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Clean technology broadens the national security base
variants.takeaway: Clean technology and space together represent more than a third of the cohort. Their prominence highlights an ecosystem whose company base extends beyond traditional defence products into energy and space capabilities.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by primary technology vertical

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Clean technology remains the broadest vertical
variants.takeaway: Removing CDC leaves clean technology and space as the largest combined concentration of companies. The breadth of these verticals is therefore a feature of the wider cohort, rather than the result of its largest financial outlier.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by primary technology vertical

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: One company shapes the federal-award picture
variants.takeaway: CDC accounts for roughly seven in ten dollars of recorded federal award value, lifting its technology, media and telecommunications vertical above the rest. Company-level concentration is therefore essential to understanding the apparent strength of that vertical.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by primary technology vertical

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Cybersecurity leads awards beyond CDC
variants.takeaway: Cybersecurity becomes the largest recipient of federal awards when CDC is removed. Clean technology has the broadest company base but a much smaller share of awards, showing that company representation does not translate evenly into government support.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by primary technology vertical

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: CDC shapes the private-capital landscape
variants.takeaway: A single company holds 45% of the cohort’s private capital, placing technology, media and telecommunications well ahead of other verticals. Clean technology and space represent broader pools of companies, highlighting the difference between financial scale and ecosystem breadth.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by primary technology vertical

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Clean technology leads capital beyond CDC
variants.takeaway: Clean technology becomes the largest pool of private capital when CDC is removed. Together with space, it accounts for almost half of the remaining investment base, placing energy and space capabilities at the centre of the wider funding picture.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by primary technology vertical

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Federal procurement is more concentrated than private capital
variants.takeaway: The five largest recipients account for 91.7% of federal contract-notice value, compared with 58.7% of private capital for the five largest fundraisers. Recorded procurement is concentrated in fewer companies than capital formation.
variants.descriptor: Cumulative shares of private capital and federal contract value by company rank

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Procurement concentration persists beyond CDC
variants.takeaway: Removing CDC reduces the dominance of the largest recipients, but contract value remains more concentrated than private capital. The five largest recipients still hold more than two-thirds of recorded contract value, showing that the pattern extends beyond one outlier.
variants.descriptor: Cumulative shares of private capital and federal contract value by company rank

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Recent fundraising is uneven across the cohort
variants.takeaway: Only about a third of companies have a recorded latest raise within the past year. The spread of fundraising dates highlights different funding timelines across the ecosystem, without establishing whether individual companies need additional capital.
variants.descriptor: Companies by time since their latest recorded capital raise

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Public markets offer another funding route
variants.takeaway: Selected 2026 listings show Australian defence technology companies accessing public equity alongside private funding. Innovaero accounts for most of the capital raised across these three examples, illustrating the range in listing scale.
variants.descriptor: Selected Australian defence IPOs and capital raised

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Selected deals connect defence technology businesses
variants.takeaway: The Penten–Amiosec merger and Shield AI’s acquisition of Sentient Vision illustrate different routes to consolidation in cybersecurity and sensing. A merger can combine businesses without taking the resulting company out of private ownership, as PentenAmio demonstrates.
variants.descriptor: Selected Australian defence mergers and acquisitions

variants.label: Original
variants.title: 31 NatSec50 companies have recorded offices outside Australia
variants.takeaway: The office tags span 23 countries, including Australia. 31 companies have a recorded presence overseas; each company counts once per country regardless of how many cities are tagged there.
variants.descriptor: Companies with a recorded office presence by country

variants.label: Original
variants.title: New South Wales anchors the NatSec50
variants.takeaway: Half the cohort is headquartered in New South Wales, making it the largest concentration of company headquarters. Victoria, the ACT, South Australia and Queensland provide additional centres of activity.
variants.descriptor: Company headquarters by state and territory

variants.label: Original
variants.title: New South Wales leads a broader office network
variants.takeaway: The cohort’s office footprint extends beyond its headquarters, with substantial company presence in Victoria and the ACT alongside New South Wales. This points to several centres of activity within the national ecosystem.
variants.descriptor: Companies with a recorded office presence by Australian state and territory

variants.label: Original
variants.title: The NatSec50 has an AUKUS-wide footprint
variants.takeaway: Recorded offices connect the cohort to all three AUKUS countries, with the US the more common overseas location. That presence provides an organisational link to partner markets, although it does not establish participation in AUKUS programmes.
variants.descriptor: Companies with a recorded office presence in AUKUS countries

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Employment growth has several leading contributors
variants.takeaway: CDC, Neara and Q-CTRL together account for just over a quarter of the cohort’s net recorded headcount gain. Their prominence is substantial, but most of the overall gain comes from the rest of the cohort.
variants.descriptor: Change in company-wide headcount, December 2022 to current 2026

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Workforce scale differs across technology areas
variants.takeaway: Autonomy and information technologies together employ more than half the recorded workforce, while quantum employment has nearly doubled since December 2022. The contrast highlights both established workforce concentrations and growth in a smaller technology area.
variants.descriptor: Company-wide headcount by critical technology area, December 2022–current 2026

variants.label: Original
variants.title: The typical NatSec50 company has grown substantially
variants.takeaway: Median recorded headcount has nearly doubled since December 2022 and is now more than five times the median across the wider eligible company pool. Growth in the typical company shows that the cohort’s expansion extends beyond its largest employers.
variants.descriptor: Median company-wide headcount, December 2022–current 2026

variants.label: Original
variants.title: NatSec50 employment outpaces the wider pool
variants.takeaway: NatSec50 headcount grew faster than the wider eligible company pool, which expanded 33.6% over the same period. The cohort’s share of recorded employment rose from 32.7% to 38.7%.
variants.descriptor: Total company-wide headcount, December 2022–current 2026

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Australia dominates the aggregate contracting picture
variants.takeaway: Recorded Australian contract values far exceed US prime obligations across the cohort, heavily influenced by CDC. Among companies already holding US prime awards, the balance reverses, showing why the aggregate alone can obscure the significance of US government work; source coverage differs.
variants.descriptor: Australian contract values and US prime obligations (AUD millions)

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Australian contract value still leads beyond CDC
variants.takeaway: Removing CDC narrows the gap substantially, but recorded Australian contract value remains 6.9 times US prime obligations. US government work is concentrated in a smaller group of companies, and the two sources have different coverage.
variants.descriptor: Australian contract values and US prime obligations (AUD millions)

variants.label: Original
variants.title: US government work reaches a limited part of the cohort
variants.takeaway: Recorded US activity is concentrated in a small group rather than spread across the NatSec50. Eight companies have prime awards, while Silentium Defence appears through subaward reports, showing that participation includes both direct and subcontracting relationships.
variants.descriptor: Recorded US prime obligations and subaward reports by company

items.label: US and Australian work by company

variants.label: Original
variants.title: US awards matter disproportionately to several companies
variants.takeaway: Six of the eight companies with US prime awards record larger US totals than Australian contract values. For this group, US government work is a substantial part of the recorded contracting picture, even though Australian value dominates the cohort-wide aggregate; source coverage differs.
variants.descriptor: US prime obligations and Australian contract values by company (AUD millions)

variants.label: Original
variants.title: DARPA anchors recorded US prime obligations
variants.takeaway: DARPA’s awards to Q-CTRL, Diraq and Silicon Quantum Computing make it the largest recorded US awarding customer. The pattern places research-oriented defence demand at the centre of the cohort’s recorded US prime activity.
variants.descriptor: US prime obligations by awarding agency (USD millions)

variants.label: Original
variants.title: A few companies lead recorded US prime activity
variants.takeaway: Q-CTRL, Hypersonix and Fivecast together account for roughly seven in ten dollars of recorded US prime obligations. The concentration shows that access to US government work is substantial for a few companies but uneven across the cohort.
variants.descriptor: US prime obligations by company (USD millions)

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Private investment has built substantial scale
variants.takeaway: The cohort combines billions in private capital with a growing workforce, but recorded federal support has not followed a steady upward path. Federal award value fell 56% in the latest completed financial year, highlighting the uneven pace of government engagement.
variants.descriptor: Private capital, federal awards, fundraising and employment indicators

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: The ecosystem extends well beyond CDC
variants.takeaway: Removing CDC still leaves billions in private investment and more than 4,500 employees across the cohort. Federal award value fell 24% in the latest completed financial year, showing that investment scale and government demand do not necessarily move together.
variants.descriptor: Private capital, federal awards, fundraising and employment indicators

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Grants reshape the NatSec50 rankings
variants.takeaway: Excluding grants shifts several companies’ rankings, highlighting those with stronger federal procurement traction.
variants.descriptor: Original rank versus contract-notice-only rank

variants.label: Original
variants.title: National security innovation spans diverse companies
variants.takeaway: The NatSec50 brings together businesses with markedly different levels of private investment and organisational maturity. Its leading ranks span space, data infrastructure and navigation, rather than a single technology niche.
variants.descriptor: Australian NatSec50 rankings and company profiles

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Public and private backers share the investment network
variants.takeaway: Main Sequence Ventures, the National Reconstruction Fund Corporation and In-Q-Tel are among the most widely connected recorded backers. The network also includes government programmes and accelerators, highlighting several forms of support around the cohort.
variants.descriptor: Recorded investors and programmes by distinct NatSec50 companies backed
